title: Infinite-Scrolling News Feed
prompt: Design the browser architecture of a personalized feed with posts, images and likes. The server supplies ranking and privacy-filtered pages. Focus on long sessions, back navigation and reliable interaction while scrolling. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Fetch cursor pages and deduplicate posts
Like a post optimistically with rollback
Preserve scroll anchor on back navigation and expose an explicit Load more action
nonFunctionalReqs: 10,000 browsed posts, 20 fetched per page; illustrative mounted window of 20 plus 10 overscan; lazy images with reserved aspect ratio.
Use semantic articles and headings, keyboard-operable like/load-more controls, polite load announcements and stable focus when rows are recycled. Never announce the whole feed on every update.
Track mutationId and server version; rollback only the failed optimistic operation. Dedup page IDs, expose retry and retain existing content.

scale.notes: 10,000 browsed posts, 20 fetched per page; illustrative mounted window of 20 plus 10 overscan; lazy images with reserved aspect ratio.
scale.storage: 10,000 posts; 30 mounted rows including overscan; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Use cursor pagination, ID normalization and a variable-height virtualized list. Anchor by post ID plus pixel offset rather than raw scrollTop. Keep new posts behind a New posts button to avoid moving the reader.
A like retry and a new page return conflicting versions
A simple paginated list has better navigation semantics for shorter feeds; virtualization helps very long sessions but complicates variable heights and accessibility.
